note: Compared with Cook's final ratings and the last public polls. Partial counts can shift a lot depending on which votes (early, mail or Election Day) are counted first.

items.title: Kansas Senate is not close so far
items.text: Hamilton (D) leads Sen. Marshall (R) 56.7%–40.7% with about 62% counted. Cook rated it a toss-up, and the final NYT/Siena poll had Hamilton up 5. No call yet.

items.title: Texas Senate margin is far above the polls
items.text: Talarico (D) leads Paxton (R) 59.0%–39.5% with about 55% counted, versus final polls showing Talarico ahead by 3 to 7. No call yet.

items.title: NY-21 leans the other way early
items.text: Gendebien (D) leads Constantino (R) 57%–43% with roughly 27% counted in a seat Cook rated Lean Republican, held by the GOP for most of the past century. No call yet.

items.title: Kentucky 6 flips
items.text: Dembo (D) was projected the winner of this open Republican-held toss-up, 55.0%–41.2% with about 92% counted.

items.title: Georgia governor flips after a tied final poll
items.text: Lance Bottoms (D) was projected the winner over Jackson (R), 54.5%–45.6% with about 81% counted. The last InsiderAdvantage poll had the race tied 49–49.

items.title: Tighter than polled: Ohio and Virginia 1
items.text: In Ohio's Senate race, Brown (D) leads Sen. Husted (R) by under 2 points with 72% counted, versus a 5-point lead in the final poll. VA-01 is essentially tied (50.2%–49.6%) with about 93% counted.
